paragraphs.title: The Psalm’s Title and Deliverance from Distress

easy.explanation: The title identifies it as a song at the dedication of the house of David.
easy.q: What is the psalm connected with according to its title?

answers: He lifted him up and healed him
He sent him into the wilderness
easy.explanation: David says that the LORD lifted him up and healed him.
easy.q: What did the LORD do for David?

easy.explanation: The passage speaks of being brought up from the grave and kept alive from the pit.
easy.q: What did the LORD save David from?

medium.explanation: David describes being lifted from a low and dangerous condition into healing and life.
medium.q: How does David describe the change the LORD made for him?

answers: Thou hast raised me from a low condition
medium.explanation: The expression describes the LORD raising David from danger and distress.
medium.q: What does “thou hast lifted me up” mean in this passage?

answers: Being brought up from the grave describes failure
medium.explanation: David mentions healing and being kept alive as parts of the LORD’s saving work.
medium.q: What is the relationship between healing and being brought up from the grave?

answers: A movement from a low place into greater danger
Deliverance from a low place and return to life
A journey from light into darkness
challenge.explanation: The expressions picture David being rescued from a low, deadly condition and restored to life.
challenge.q: What central image is created by “thou hast lifted me up” and “brought up my soul from the grave”?

answers: Distress and danger versus healing and life
challenge.explanation: David moves from danger and the grave to healing, preservation, and praise.
challenge.q: What is the main contrast between David’s condition at the beginning and after the LORD’s deliverance?

answers: The verses focus mainly on deliverance from distress
The verses contain no reference to a house
The verses concern only David’s enemies
challenge.explanation: Although the title mentions the dedication of the house, these verses focus on David’s healing and deliverance.
challenge.q: Why can the passage be said to contain more than the subject of its title?

paragraphs.title: Thanksgiving for the Change from Weeping to Joy

easy.explanation: David says, “Sing unto the LORD, O ye saints of his.”
easy.q: Whom does David call to sing unto the LORD?

answers: At the remembrance of his holiness
At the remembrance of his wars
At the remembrance of his journeys
easy.explanation: The verse says to give thanks at the remembrance of the LORD’s holiness.
easy.q: For what should they give thanks?

easy.explanation: David says, “joy cometh in the morning.”
easy.q: What does the morning bring in this passage?

answers: Weeping may be followed by joy
Night is always longer than day
medium.explanation: The verse contrasts weeping during the night with joy coming in the morning.
medium.q: What does the contrast between night and morning teach?

medium.explanation: Joy means gladness, happiness, and rejoicing.
medium.q: What does “joy” mean in “joy cometh in the morning”?

answers: His favour is connected with life
medium.explanation: The verse says, “in his favour is life.”
medium.q: What does the verse say about the LORD’s favour?

answers: Deliverance leads people to thank the LORD
Joy represents turning away from the LORD
challenge.explanation: The experience of deliverance and renewed joy provides reason to give thanks to the LORD.
challenge.q: How does the call to give thanks fit with the change from weeping to joy?

answers: The LORD’s anger is brief compared with the life found in his favour
challenge.explanation: The verse places a brief moment of anger against the lasting blessing of life in the LORD’s favour.
challenge.q: What is the meaning of “his anger endureth but a moment” in context?

challenge.explanation: The verse associates night with weeping and morning with joy.
challenge.q: Which pairing correctly reflects the images in the verse?

paragraphs.title: From Tranquility to Fear and Prayer

easy.explanation: David says, “in my prosperity I said, I shall never be moved.”
easy.q: In what condition did David say he would never be moved?

easy.explanation: David says, “thou didst hide thy face, and I was troubled.”
easy.q: What happened when David felt that the LORD had hidden His face?

answers: He cried unto the LORD and made supplication
easy.explanation: David cried to the LORD and pleaded with Him.
easy.q: What did David do when he was troubled?

answers: His feeling that the LORD had hidden His face
medium.explanation: David connects his trouble with the LORD hiding His face.
medium.q: What caused David’s change from confidence to trouble?

medium.explanation: In this context, troubled means distressed, alarmed, or afraid.
medium.q: What does “troubled” mean in “I was troubled”?

medium.explanation: David first describes prosperity, then the hidden face of the LORD, his trouble, and his prayer.
medium.q: What is the order of events in the passage?

answers: His confidence depended on his relationship with the LORD
challenge.explanation: The contrast shows that David’s confidence was shaken when he felt separated from the LORD’s favour.
challenge.q: What does the change from “I shall never be moved” to “I was troubled” reveal about David’s confidence?

answers: His distress leads him to call upon the LORD
He has already received everything he requested
He wants to move away from the LORD
challenge.explanation: David responds to his trouble by crying to the LORD and making supplication.
challenge.q: Why does prayer appear immediately after David describes his trouble?

answers: Both describe an earnest appeal to the LORD
Both describe going down into the pit
challenge.explanation: The two expressions emphasize David’s urgent and humble prayer.
challenge.q: What connection exists between “I cried” and “I made supplication”?

paragraphs.title: A Plea for Life and the Transformation of Mourning into Joy

easy.explanation: David asks what profit there would be in his blood when he goes down to the pit.
easy.q: From what does David ask to be spared?

easy.explanation: David says, “Thou hast turned for me my mourning into dancing.”
easy.q: What did the LORD turn David’s mourning into?

answers: Give thanks to the LORD for ever
easy.explanation: David concludes, “I will give thanks unto thee for ever.”
easy.q: What does David promise to do at the end of the psalm?

answers: So that he can praise the LORD and declare His truth
So that he can avoid singing
So that he can hide his distress
medium.explanation: David asks whether the dust can praise or declare the LORD’s truth, emphasizing the value of life for worship.
medium.q: Why does David ask to remain alive?

medium.explanation: Profit here means benefit, advantage, or gain.
medium.q: What does “profit” mean in “What profit is there in my blood”?

answers: A change from sorrow and mourning to joy
A change from joy to silence
A change from prayer to anger
medium.explanation: The LORD transforms David’s signs of mourning into dancing and gladness.
medium.q: What change is described by “mourning into dancing” and “sackcloth ... with gladness”?

answers: A living person can praise the LORD and declare His truth
Life is unnecessary for giving thanks
The grave is a place of joy
challenge.explanation: David emphasizes that he can praise and proclaim the LORD’s truth while he is alive.
challenge.q: What is David’s main point in asking about going down to the pit?

answers: His plea for life ends with a promise to give thanks forever
His plea ends with turning away from the LORD
His plea ends by returning to fear
challenge.explanation: After asking for mercy and help, David responds to deliverance with a lasting promise of praise.
challenge.q: How does the ending connect with David’s plea earlier in the passage?

answers: A plea for life, the LORD’s answer, mourning turned to joy, and thanksgiving
Joy, silence, descent into the pit, and fear
The hidden face, dancing, mourning, and hopelessness
challenge.explanation: David pleads for mercy, describes the LORD’s transforming help, and ends by promising continual praise.
challenge.q: What is the central sequence in this passage?
